label: Oslo — Grünerløkka historic masonry grid
scope: Authored historic residential core from Sannergata to the Schous/Nordre-gate area, including Birkelunden, Olav Ryes plass and the photographed Helgesens frontages. Boundaries follow selected mapped streets and connect nearby street anchors. This is not the modern administrative borough or the legal Birkelunden conservation boundary.

weight_basis.construction: Riksantikvaren describes closed masonry apartment blocks as dominant in Grünerløkka. Its Birkelunden conservation subset documents 15 blocks and 139 apartment buildings; that count is not extrapolated as a full district census. Representative street, courtyard, Markveien and aerial photos support common plastered masonry, secondary exposed brick, simpler courtyard fabric and occasional modern infill.
weight_basis.finishes: Neutral/ochre plaster is common across the inspected rows, with salmon and green alternatives and coordinated trim/joinery. Red brick with pale masonry detailing is a secondary actual Markveien example. Red clay tiles are directly visible in the courtyard; aerial red/dark roof choices remain qualitative. Common district character is extrapolated between samples; no exact block percentages are claimed.

label: Milan: central historic fabric and modern apartments
scope: The central Nucleo di Antica Formazione polygon (Comune di Milano current PGT R04 objectid 11), including Brera and the central Ticinese/Navigli approach. weight_basis.construction: Relative priorities retain the warm rendered, shuttered clay-roof apartment rows visible in Brera and Navigli, cream more formally framed apartments, and explicit plain twentieth-century replacements.
